items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: I went to a concert of Ellington music... And Gunther Schuller was conducting.

ctx.x: I like some of the musicians that have talked about the fact that when they were playing back in the 30s and 40s that the amplification was not an issue really. So they played perhaps a little more attuned to each other. If you were in the back row and you couldn’t hear the soloist, then you were playing too loud, and it wasn’t a matter of turn up his microphone—

You are absolutely my man on that. I absolutely agree with you. I went to a concert of Ellington music in Milwaukee at the Performing Arts Center, which is a gorgeous, © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -17-

modern, I guess they do symphony concerts there and so forth. And Gunther Schuller was conducting. And just before the concert started, he walked around the stage and pulled out every plug. He said, “we’ll have none of this.” And it was just wonderful. God it sounded like the way it was supposed to sound.
